description: Mortar is an open testbed for portable building analytics developed at UC Berkeley and LBNL, described in a 2020 ACM Transactions on Sensor Networks paper. At publication it spanned 90 buildings and more than 9.1 billion data points, with every building described using the Brick metadata schema so that analytics can find the sensors, equipment and systems they need by meaning, not by hard-coded point names. The authors proposed an architecture for portable analytics applications that configure themselves from building context and demonstrated it by implementing 11 applications from the literature. Coverage: mostly commercial buildings in the United States. Access: the Mortar website and API; the site's TLS certificate had expired when checked here, so access could not be confirmed. Licence: not read. Caveats: the project may no longer be maintained; related Brick models and data may be available from the authors or later projects. Simulation uses are testing fault detection, energy analytics and control applications across many HVAC systems described in Brick. Related records: the Brick schema and the Building Data Genome 2.
